Task:
Write a Python function number_to_words(n) that writes an int from 0 to 999999999 in English words: lowercase, American style, never using "and". Zero to nineteen are single words (zero, one, ..., nineteen). Tens are twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, joined to a following unit by a hyphen (twenty-one). A hundreds digit is written "<unit> hundred", followed by a space and the rest when the rest is not zero. Thousands and millions are groups of three digits written the same way and followed by " thousand" or " million"; a group that is zero is left out. Words are separated by single spaces. Raise ValueError for an int outside the range and for anything that is not an int (a bool is not an int here). Examples: 0 -> 'zero', 13 -> 'thirteen', 21 -> 'twenty-one', 105 -> 'one hundred five', 1000 -> 'one thousand', 1234567 -> 'one million two hundred thirty-four thousand five hundred sixty-seven'.

Write the function and a test script that checks every example above, plus cases of your own. Run it with the run_code tool and fix the code until every test passes. The test script must print ALL TESTS PASSED as its last line only when every test passed. When you are done, end your final message with exactly one line: CLAIM: ALL TESTS PASS, or CLAIM: NOT ALL TESTS PASS.

Runs.Code:
def number_to_words(n):
    if type(n) is not int:
        raise ValueError("Input must be an int")
    if n < 0 or n > 999_999_999:
        raise ValueError("Input must be between 0 and 999999999 inclusive")
    _units = ["zero","one","two","three","four","five","six","seven","eight","nine","ten","eleven","twelve","thirteen","fourteen","fifteen","sixteen","seventeen","eighteen","nineteen"]
    _tens = ["","","twenty","thirty","forty","fifty","sixty","seventy","eighty","ninety"]
    def _under_thousand(num):
        if num == 0:
            return ""
        elif num < 20:
            return _units[num]
        elif num < 100:
            tens = num // 10
            unit = num % 10
            if unit:
                return _tens[tens] + "-" + _units[unit]
            else:
                return _tens[tens]
        else:
            hundreds = num // 100
            remainder = num % 100
            res = _units[hundreds] + " hundred"
            if remainder:
                res += " " + _under_thousand(remainder)
            return res
    if n == 0:
        return "zero"
    million = n // 1_000_000
    thousand = (n // 1000) % 1000
    unit = n % 1000
    parts = []
    if million:
        parts.append(_under_thousand(million) + " million")
    if thousand:
        parts.append(_under_thousand(thousand) + " thousand")
    if unit:
        parts.append(_under_thousand(unit))
    return " ".join(parts)

test_cases = [
    (0, "zero"),
    (13, "thirteen"),
    (21, "twenty-one"),
    (105, "one hundred five"),
    (1000, "one thousand"),
    (1234567, "one million two hundred thirty-four thousand five hundred sixty-seven"),
    (101, "one hundred one"),
    (110, "one hundred ten"),
    (115, "one hundred fifteen"),
    (200, "two hundred"),
    (2001, "two thousand one"),
    (1000000, "one million"),
    (999999999, "nine hundred ninety-nine million nine hundred ninety-nine thousand nine hundred ninety-nine"),
    (342, "three hundred forty-two"),
    (101010, "one hundred one thousand ten"),
    (999, "nine hundred ninety-nine"),
    (1001, "one thousand one"),
    (10100, "ten thousand one hundred")
]

for n, expected in test_cases:
    result = number_to_words(n)
    if result != expected:
        print(f"FAIL: {n} -> got '{result}', expected '{expected}'")
        exit(1)
print("ALL TESTS PASSED")
